newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen firmer on high-techs and banks.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen firmer on high-techs and banks.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to trade firmer on Wednesday as bullish technology shares in New York and the yen's decline against the dollar will stimulate buying momentum in blue-chip high-tech issues in Tokyo, brokers said.

News late on Tuesday that the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) would form a strategic alliance would support LTCB shares, and probably shares of other banks as well, they said.
On Tuesday, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,069.41, down 159.31 points or 0.79 percent. Its September futures slipped 170 points to end at 20,070.
But brokers said the upside of the key stock index would be limited by strong profit-taking interest.

"I expect the Nikkei 225 to show a pretty good performance, but the upside may be capped by profit-taking," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager of the equities operations group at Nikko Securities Co Ltd. He said he expected the Nikkei index to range between 20,000 and 20,300.

The news of LTCB's cooperation with SBC is likely to touch off expectations that other Japanese banks may form global strategic alliances with foreign banks, which would support bank shares in Tokyo, brokers said.
In early morning Tokyo, the dollar was trading at around 115.50 yen, against around 114.15 yen in late Tokyo trade on Tuesday.
On Tuesday in New York, the Nasdaq composite index posted its ninth consecutive record high, gaining 18.25 points or 1.20 percent to close at 1,542.12.
